liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Called the best Jack Straw of 1984, with Lesh's heavy bass driving and Garcia chasing him [12]
- **Cold Rain and Snow** (1 review): Mydland's B-3 organ adds a lot to it [12]
- **New Minglewood Blues** (1 review): The Minglewood jam is described as inspired and lengthy [12]
- **Touch Of Grey** (1 review): Phil whispered to Jerry, prompting Touch of Grey; first non-Scarlet/Fire pairing in seven years [17]
- **Terrapin Station** (1 review): Great Terrapin, including an odd warrior-like sound effect coming from Brent [14]
- **Drums** (1 review): Drums/space is wild, with Ken Kesey and Babs involved [14]

## Setlist highlights

- **This place got mice**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **Jerry Jam**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **The Thunder Machine**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **Bob's Thank You**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]

## The recordings

- **gd1984-05-08.sonyecm.andrewf.29304.sbefail.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 25 songs; 171 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [1]. Said about its sound: Audience recording sounds distant with heavy crowd noise, taped from far back under the mezzanine roof [1]
- **gd1984-05-08.134627.mtx.seamons.ht109.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 169 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [2]
- **gd1984-05-08.152058.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac1648**: audience recording; 21 songs; 180 min [3]
- **gd84-05-08.sbd.lai.2573.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 161 min; rated 4.11/5 by 18 [5]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the recording has no static, scratches or digital pops, contradicting an earlier reviewer; Some static on the third disc, mildly annoying in The Other One, end of Wharf Rat, Miracle and Dew; Classic 1984 sound; Brent's keyboards sound great, compensating for Jerry being low in the mix [14][15][18]
- **gd1984-05-08.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.77312.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 21 songs; 162 min; rated 2.33/5 by 6 [7]. Said about its sound: Terrapin has the same noise as the other soundboard, but this version is far clearer, with deep bass [23]

## Around the show

- Stage talk about: Other One [1]
- Attendee on one side of the hall heard static from the PA; friends on the other side didn't [17]
- Attendee saw all three shows in the run; considers this one a fond memory [22]
- Thunder Machine was wheeled out; taper flipped tapes then, finishing before Morning Dew began [1]
- Drums featured Ken Kesey and the Thunder Machine [2]
- Ken Kesey played the Thunder Machine [3]
- Said to be the first time in seven years that Scarlet wasn't followed by Fire [17]
- Reviewer calls it run of the mill for 1984, with several other 1984 shows far superior [21]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1984-05-08.sonyecm.andrewf.29304.sbefail.flac16**: taped by Andrew F.; source: Sony ECM-939LT stereo mic > Marantz PMD-340 cassette deck. Sony UCX-S 90 cassettes, with Dolby B On > MAC > Sony TC-D5M > Marantz CDR-500 > EAC > Soundforge >… [1]. Also: Taped with a Sony ECM; uploader released it because the circulating soundboard is muffled and has static [1]
- **gd1984-05-08.134627.mtx.seamons.ht109.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix by Hunter Seamons using Final Cut Pro (FLAC > AIFF > Final Cut > Soundtrack > AIFF CD tracking via Audacity > FLAC16 via xACT w/meta-tagging) [2]. Also: Matrix mix; soundboard speed fluctuated heavily from Terrapin Station onward, making the correction three times harder [2]
- **gd1984-05-08.152058.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Mark Severson; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Mark Severson's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics > Sony D5M [3]
- **gd84-05-08.sbd.lai.2573.sbefail.shnf**: source: SBD> MR> C> DAT> CDR [5]
- **gd1984-05-08.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.77312.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Transferred/Edited by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Cassette (Nakamichi 550/Maxell XLIIS-90) > Cassette (Sony TC-WE475) -> Sony R500 (Pass Through) -> SEK'D Prodif Plus -> Samplitude… [7]. Also: Soundboard from cassettes provided by Paul Scotton and Joani Walker, with patch source from Gary Field [7]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Jerry Garcia: [1984-05-08 Backstage Pass - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1984-05-08-backstage-pass/) [25]
- Poster by Steve Schneider Grateful Dead: [1984-05-07 Silva Hall, Hult Center, Eugene, OR, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1984-05-07-silva-hall-hult-center-eugene-or-usa/) [26]
- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1984-05-08 Ticket - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1984-05-08-ticket/) [27]
